record.original_question: Let H be a separable infinite-dimensional complex Hilbert space and let T be a bounded complex symmetric operator on H, meaning T = C T* C for some conjugation C. Must T have an invariant subspace that is both proper and nontrivial, that is, a subspace other than {0} and H that is mapped into itself by T?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $H$ be a separable infinite-dimensional complex Hilbert space. A conjugation on $H$ is a map $C:H\to H$ that is antilinear, isometric (i.e., $\langle Cx,Cy\rangle=\langle y,x\rangle$ for all $x,y\in H$), and involutive ($C^2=I$). A bounded linear operator $T$ on $H$ is called complex symmetric if there exists a conjugation $C$ on $H$ such that $T=CT^*C$.

Question: Must every bounded complex symmetric operator $T$ on $H$ possess a nontrivial proper invariant closed subspace, i.e., a closed subspace $M\subset H$ with $M\neq\{0\}$ and $M\neq H$ such that $T(M)\subseteq M$?
artifact.status_search_result: The general invariant subspace problem for bounded operators on a separable infinite-dimensional complex Hilbert space remains open (a 2023 preprint of Enflo claiming a positive solution has not been broadly verified). The restriction of the problem to the class of complex symmetric operators is not known to be settled either; it is highlighted as an open question in surveys on complex symmetric operators.

status_evidence.snippet: The invariant subspace problem for separable Hilbert spaces is a long-standing open problem in functional analysis.
status_evidence.claim: The general Hilbert space invariant subspace problem remains open as of recent surveys.

status_evidence.title: On the invariant subspace problem in Hilbert spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Enflo's 2023 preprint claims a positive solution for Hilbert spaces, but verification is ongoing.
status_evidence.claim: A claimed proof exists but has not been fully accepted, leaving the status effectively open.

status_evidence.title: The invariant subspace problem in Hilbert spaces – SPP 2026
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of the still-open status of the invariant subspace problem on Hilbert spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Restricted classes such as complex symmetric operators continue to be studied as open subcases.
